data.title: A 12-year sequence of telescope images of a star and four planets orbiting
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕直接成像的系外行星轨道动画，讨论其真实性、制作方法、科学意义、观测局限及未来技术。

不同观点：
• 技术与数据：wthomp展示仅使用凯克望远镜、同一仪器和3.5微米波段制作的动画；原GIF则综合了不同望远镜和波长。  
• 真实性争议：hatthew指出动画只有约10张静态图，其余数百帧为插值生成，并非连续实拍；但仍具有展示价值。  
• 观测前景：ortusdux期待罗曼空间望远镜日冕仪，称其灵敏度将提升100—1000倍，可直接拍摄类似木星的行星；7373737373补充宜居世界天文台未来或能发现类地行星。  
• 科学意义：alexpotato指出现代搜寻技术已将“拥有行星的恒星比例”从原先低估修正到接近100%；sixothree以科学史变化强调系外行星发现的突破。  
• 公众传播：tocs3认为科学图像虽未必总是研究重点，却是非专业公众理解科学的重要途径；其他评论推荐银河系中心恒星绕黑洞运行等相关动画。

补充讨论：评论者还追问观测间隔、恒星遮挡噪声变化、行星角距，以及是否存在被大型行星“遮蔽”的更小行星；争议焦点主要是动画的“实拍程度”及图像变化究竟源于天体活动还是观测技术改进。

data.title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 美国犹他州SB73要求成人网站识别并阻断使用VPN的用户、进行年龄验证，甚至禁止提供绕过指南。EFF认为该法侵犯隐私、造成州外用户和企业负担，并要求技术上不可能的精准定位。联邦法官据此发布初步禁令，暂缓执行相关条款，认定其可能违宪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：犹他州要求网站验证用户年龄、限制VPN绕过访问的法律，是否可行、合法，以及州政府管辖互联网的边界。

不同观点：
• 技术不可行论：VPN流量难以可靠识别，用户可通过普通云主机、自建隧道或代理绕过；按域名过滤也容易失效。有人认为该法要求“技术不可能”，立法者缺乏技术常识。  
• 可执行论：反驳者指出，DraftKings等赌博网站能通过账户、支付和位置验证限制特定州用户，因此并非完全无法实施，但自建VPN等方式仍很难封堵。  
• 自由与宪法争议：禁止网站提供VPN绕过教程被质疑侵犯第一修正案；也有人认为州无权管辖州外服务器，需挑战其互联网管辖权。  
• 反审查立场：有人警告这是政府扩大网络控制的开端，色情限制只是表面理由；“互联网总会绕过审查”并非定律，中国、伊朗等案例表明监控、自我审查和SNI封锁能有效压制访问，维护开放网络需要主动行动。  
• 州政策辩护：犹他州禁赌，限制VPN以执行赌博禁令在逻辑上自洽；支持者称赌博会带来成瘾、债务、家庭暴力和治安问题，因此州应有一定执法空间。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于公共利益与个人网络自由的平衡，以及州级法律能否、是否应当跨越技术和地域边界执行。

49927754.article_content:
Español
When state lawmakers attempt to rewrite how the internet works, users rely on courts to recognize that laws can’t make technical impossibilities a reality. That’s why we were happy to see that a court has blocked Utah’s attempt to outlaw the privacy protections of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs).
In a win for digital rights, a federal judge has
issued a preliminary injunction
blocking Utah’s SB 73, the state’s draconian
anti-VPN age verification law
. The decision comes as EFF
submitted our comments
to the Utah Department of Commerce, detailing how forcing platforms to detect and block privacy-preserving tools undermines user privacy and security worldwide while demanding the impossible.
What SB 73 Does
Signed
into law earlier this year
, SB 73 attempted to regulate adult websites by requiring them to block VPN users or to identify the physical location of visitors using them or similar tools that mask their network traffic. It even went so far as to prohibit websites from offering instructions on how to use a VPN to bypass these checks. This made Utah, to EFF’s knowledge, the first state in the nation to target the use of VPNs to avoid legally mandated age-verification gates.
The Utah federal court
halted enforcement
of the law's VPN provisions last week,
r
uling that the law likely violates the U.S. Constitution’s prohibition on passing laws that significantly burden businesses and people outside Utah’s borders.
SB 73 burdens the rights of all internet users outside of Utah because it requires adult websites to either know every visiting user’s physical location, and then block those in Utah, or to verify every visitor’s age just in case they might be in Utah. The law’s “actual-location provision in practice requires an entity to perform age verification services for every user visiting its site from any location because the entity would violate the law if even one of those users happened to be obfuscating,” the court wrote. The court essentially ruled that Utah has less-burdensome ways to prevent Utah minors from accessing adult websites than requiring all users in the world to comply with SB 73.
Aylo’s lawsuit does not challenge SB 73’s provision prohibiting the websites covered by the law from sharing information about VPNs.
The Legal Challenge
This court order follows months of legal maneuvering.
Initially set to
go into effect in May 2026
, SB 73 sparked an
immediate constitutional challenge from Aylo
, the parent company of major online adult platforms like Pornhub. In response to the lawsuit, Utah and Aylo
initially agreed
that the state would pause enforcement while the court considered the preliminary injunction request
or
until administrative rules setting specific compliance terms were finalized. Those proposed compliance rules (R152-78B, see
Utah State Bulletin, page 6
) were published by the Utah Department of Commerce’s Division of Consumer Protection on September 1
st
, and EFF
submitted formal comments
to the Department in opposition. According to the notice, the proposed rules could be effective as soon as October 8, 2026. However, Judge Barlow’s decision means that it cannot be enforced pending further action by the court.
The Ruling
EFF welcomes Judge Barlow’s ruling, which recognizes the fundamental disconnect between state legislation of the internet and how technology works. In his ruling, Judge Barlow noted that the statute requires a technical impossibility on pain of legal liability. “Aylo is correct that the statute, as amended, now essentially imposes strict liability for entities like it when it comes to determining the location of its websites’ users.”
The court recognized that the problem is that SB 73 “requires entities like Aylo to geolocate its website users with perfection to avoid liability.” But, at the same time, the court acknowledged “that geolocation perfection is not presently possible.”
EFF explained this technical impossibility in
our comment to the Department of Commerce.
VPNs protect user privacy by routing web traffic through intermediary servers. Because destination websites only see the IP address of the VPN server, they have no reliable mechanism to tell whether a connection originates from Salt Lake City, Seattle, or Shanghai. So, under Utah's current statutory framework, platforms are left with an impossible choice: completely block all VPN traffic nationwide or withdraw access from Utah entirely. Judge Barlow agreed, asserting:
Because the law requires perfection in the absence of perfect geolocation tools, Aylo would need to verify those 28 million users—whether located in Salt Lake City, Boston, New Orleans, Anchorage, or Honolulu—to ensure compliance and avoid liability.
The Rulemaking
The administrative rules drafted by the state compelled commercial entities to implement "commercially reasonable geolocation obfuscation detection systems", which is a directive, we argue, that demands a technical impossibility.

data.title: Mike Tomlin spent 12 years building a Minecraft city
data.author: CoryOndrejka
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：前NFL教练迈克·汤姆林花12年在《我的世界》中用手柄建造城市，引发对个人兴趣、创造意义、投入方式及其职业表现的讨论。

不同观点：
• 多数评论赞赏其投入与真诚，认为即使不懂《我的世界》或橄榄球，也能感受到长期创作带来的快乐；有人称其“感人、温暖”，甚至建议匹兹堡聘他做城市规划顾问。  
• 有人强调作品的意义不在技术难度。虽然熟练玩家、程序或AI可能更快生成类似城市，但这是他在自身限制下亲手完成、体现个人思想的作品，可视为AI时代“为兴趣而做”的例子。  
• 也有人钦佩其耐心：他使用手柄且灵敏度较低，耗时可能是PC操作的两倍；考虑到他曾是长期保持胜绩的NFL主教练，这种业余投入尤其不可思议。  
• 调侃或质疑其职业取舍的观点认为，他开始建城后季后赛战绩从5胜3负降至3胜9负，球员甚至开玩笑说球队在争超级碗时教练却在玩Minecraft。  
• 部分玩家更偏好自动化，认为重复建造繁琐，AI或模组可生成主体、让孩子添加细节，但这可能破坏生存模式的平衡。

补充讨论：评论借电影台词讨论“何时回归真正让自己快乐的事”，并批评“成年人玩游戏很丢脸”的社会偏见；也有人认为若基本生活有保障，人们或许能更多从事这类非功利创作。

data.title: Loss of cell identity drives human aging: Two new papers
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕胚胎表观遗传重置及相关论文，讨论衰老是否可逆、其机制是损伤积累还是进化编程，以及研究的局限。

不同观点：
• **表观遗传重置支持部分可逆性**：胚胎受精后可清除父源DNA上的年龄相关化学标记、重塑染色质、重建端粒并清理受损蛋白，但无法修复精子累积的DNA突变；有人据此将生物系统理解为“信息系统”。
• **强调证据边界**：线粒体重置主要针对父源线粒体；母源线粒体通常不会被重置，少数父源线粒体遗传的影响仍不清楚。
• **质疑“损伤/漂移”模型**：有评论认为论文只是给累积损伤假说换了包装，未解释Hayflick极限、不同物种寿命差异等，并主张衰老和死亡是为适应进化而被程序化的核心机制。
• **折中或相反假说**：表观遗传衰老可能是对DNA损伤的适应性、程序化反应，类似病毒症状主要由免疫反应造成，而非病毒直接造成。

补充讨论：有人指出慢性压力可能加速衰老，并询问定点甲基化/去甲基化技术；也有人认为研究忽略了连接不同时间尺度的昼夜节律。另有评论关注论文未充分讨论新的Hayflick极限，以及批评网页使用AI插图而削弱信息价值。

data.title: From the creator of Redis; run LLM locally with ds4
data.author: fibo
data.article_summary: 文章介绍 ds4，一款用 C 编写的本地推理引擎，支持 DeepSeek V4/V4.1、GLM 5.x 和 Qwen3.8 等模型，兼容 Apple Silicon、CUDA 与 ROCm。其核心技术包括非对称 2-bit 量化、SSD 持久化 KV 缓存、张量并行和视觉输入，并提供 CLI、OpenAI/Anthropic API 及编程代理，适合高内存设备本地运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ds4 面向苹果芯片等消费级硬件的本地大模型推理，强调“覆盖主要用例、再进行专业化扩展”的软件设计理念，以及模型、性能和硬件适配。

不同观点：
• 设计理念支持者认为，AI时代开源软件应先服务通用场景，不必试图覆盖所有配置，后续可由用户和社区定制。有人将其与Redis的简洁、低依赖哲学相提并论。  
• 使用者普遍评价积极：ds4在M5 Max 128GB上运行DeepSeek、Qwen等模型速度快、上下文长，是优秀的本地模型启动器；但也有人反馈模型偶尔忘记早先内容，可能与Agent框架有关。  
• 社区扩展者提供了Go共享库、FFI、多种工具、Vision/Qwen支持及Homebrew安装方式，体现出围绕ds4进行语言绑定和功能专业化的生态路线。  
• 硬件适配存在分歧：高端Mac（96GB以上）更适合Metal直跑，较小内存设备可依靠SSD streaming；64GB设备能运行部分模型，但大型完整模型仍有压力。  
• 其他方案包括面向Intel Xe-LP的xenolith、支持高端Apple Silicon的Local Code，以及面向3090/Qwen 27B的club-3090，说明本地推理生态正在分化。  

补充讨论：用户关注64GB以下的实际速度、工具调用效果、能否达到约50 TPS，以及模型专用内核与通用推理引擎的技术差异；也有人计划移植更快的Metal kernel。

49936575.article_summary: 文章介绍 ds4，一款用 C 编写的本地推理引擎，支持 DeepSeek V4/V4.1、GLM 5.x 和 Qwen3.8 等模型，兼容 Apple Silicon、CUDA 与 ROCm。其核心技术包括非对称 2-bit 量化、SSD 持久化 KV 缓存、张量并行和视觉输入，并提供 CLI、OpenAI/Anthropic API 及编程代理，适合高内存设备本地运行。
49936575.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ds4 面向苹果芯片等消费级硬件的本地大模型推理，强调“覆盖主要用例、再进行专业化扩展”的软件设计理念，以及模型、性能和硬件适配。

不同观点：
• 设计理念支持者认为，AI时代开源软件应先服务通用场景，不必试图覆盖所有配置，后续可由用户和社区定制。有人将其与Redis的简洁、低依赖哲学相提并论。  
• 使用者普遍评价积极：ds4在M5 Max 128GB上运行DeepSeek、Qwen等模型速度快、上下文长，是优秀的本地模型启动器；但也有人反馈模型偶尔忘记早先内容，可能与Agent框架有关。  
• 社区扩展者提供了Go共享库、FFI、多种工具、Vision/Qwen支持及Homebrew安装方式，体现出围绕ds4进行语言绑定和功能专业化的生态路线。  
• 硬件适配存在分歧：高端Mac（96GB以上）更适合Metal直跑，较小内存设备可依靠SSD streaming；64GB设备能运行部分模型，但大型完整模型仍有压力。  
• 其他方案包括面向Intel Xe-LP的xenolith、支持高端Apple Silicon的Local Code，以及面向3090/Qwen 27B的club-3090，说明本地推理生态正在分化。  

补充讨论：用户关注64GB以下的实际速度、工具调用效果、能否达到约50 TPS，以及模型专用内核与通用推理引擎的技术差异；也有人计划移植更快的Metal kernel。

data.author: usernomdeguerre
data.article_summary: 该内容为 YouTube 网站页脚信息，包含关于、新闻、版权、联系方式、创作者、广告、开发者、服务条款、隐私政策、安全政策、平台运作方式及 NFL Sunday Ticket 等链接，并注明“© 2026 Google LLC”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Anthropic 的 Mythos 利用大模型发现 Linux 内核漏洞的宣传，评论者讨论其实际价值、技术能力、可信度及法律风险。

不同观点：
• **质疑过度宣传**：多位评论者引用 Greg KH 的说法，认为79个“漏洞”中大量不是漏洞、已有修复或条件极端，最终真正需要处理的约10个，修复工作约一小时；因此认为 Anthropic 将静态模式匹配包装成重大安全突破，损害自身信誉。  
• **批评方法与署名**：Mythos主要是将历史补丁中的修复模式套用到其他代码，并未体现深入分析；Anthropic也没有充分引用最初发现和修复漏洞的内核开发者，类似“AI不尊重原创”的问题。  
• **谨慎看好长期潜力**：有人认为当前 Mythos确实被夸大，但专门训练、配合代码地图、威胁模型和验证工具的模型，未来可能提高漏洞发现、分析和修复效率；多个模型交叉复核或许能降低误报。  
• **强调人工审查不可替代**：报告生成成本几乎为零，但验证成本未下降；模型易迎合用户、输出错误解释，不能取代资深开发者，甚至已干扰技术协作。  
• **法律与隐私担忧**：讨论延伸至训练数据的版权合法性、Linux项目如何应对潜在诉讼，以及免费模型可能泄露用户提交的非公开信息。

补充讨论：争议核心是“模型发现了多少真实且有价值的新漏洞”，以及企业宣传是否掩盖了误报、重复劳动和验证成本。

data.title: FLUX 3 Image
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种通过边界框布局生成图像的方法。用户可在横纵坐标均为0至1000的画布上精确安排元素，选择画布比例，并结合场景提示词生成图像。文中还展示了多个示例主题及生成结果，支持回放和重新调整。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Flux 3 Image（或其界面）的可控编辑能力、实际效果、开放性与评测方式展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **UX/可控性受肯定**：多人认为通过框选、指定位置进行局部编辑，操作直观且可精细迭代；有人用它替换截图中的 UI 元素，首次成功率较高，并称其界面优于纯聊天式交互。  
• **模型效果褒贬不一**：部分示例表现优秀，但“衬衫印刷”案例被批评为明显糟糕；乐器键盘、马与栅栏等复杂细节或局部编辑也可能失败，小文字仍易被打乱。  
• **与既有方案比较**：Ideogram V4 也支持按区域布局，但需要繁琐 JSON 描述边界框，因此该产品的交互更友好；不过有人质疑这究竟是新模型还是新 UI。  
• **开放权重诉求**：评论者普遍期待尽快开放权重、支持本地运行，类似 Flux/Klein；也有人赞赏美国、中国之外的团队推出高质量模型。  
• **应用需求仍未满足**：游戏开发者关心能否生成高保真、逐帧一致的 sprite 序列，目前仍需“参考图→短视频→抽帧”的变通流程。  
• **评测与比较困难**：有人询问如何客观比较 Qwen、Flux、Midjourney 等图像/视频模型，反映现有基准不足。

补充讨论：有人调侃 AI 图像已“解决”并导致数字证据失去可信度；另有用户关注 OpenRouter 的限时五折价格。

data.title: One month coding with GLM 5.3 Flash
data.author: ThibWeb
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了9月只使用一种高效开源模型的挑战：目标模型仅承担约50%的使用量，2B tokens中有1B转向其他模型，能耗约35kWh，挑战未达成。主要原因包括原型开发选错模型导致高额消耗、推理基础设施容量不足，以及研发实验需测试多种模型。作者计划加强本地监测、为实验单独预算、优化多智能体协作，并推动日常工作更多采用低成本、低能耗模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“整月使用单一低价开放模型”的挑战，讨论模型性价比、代理式开发成本、文章表述及评测方法。

不同观点：
• **批评文章**：开头像标题党，让人以为文章要证明廉价模型性能不足；实际重点却是开发流程和模型选择失误，内容含糊、缺乏失败案例，也未说明为何选错模型、何者更好，因此被批评为浪费时间。  
• **肯定 GLM 5.3 Flash**：多位评论者认为它便宜、快速且能力强，适合日常编码、模糊需求修复和作为代理默认模型；有人认为其体验接近 Opus 4.5，但一致性仍略逊，Qwen 新版也可能更省资源。  
• **成本与预算观点**：一个月代理式编码仅约68美元，说明模型选择已同时是质量和预算决策；但原型因选错模型一夜消耗4.5亿token、150美元，理论上可用约五分之一成本完成，凸显需预估token消耗并谨慎设计agent流程。  
• **评测方法质疑**：只比较“每token成本”不够，还应考察完成任务所需token数、速度，以及每项任务的实际成本和耗时。  
• **原型开发观点**：AI适合快速试错和复杂原型，但首版往往应被丢弃，不宜直接用于高风险生产系统。

补充讨论：有人惊讶4kWh能耗极低，并据此推测AI数据中心建设可能过度扩张；也有人怀疑高额消耗与缓存失效或未补贴的推理服务有关。

49934620.article_content:
Setting a challenge to spend the
whole of September on only one efficient open model
felt like a great idea at the time. Turns out not so much in practice. 2B tokens later, here’s how it went.
Where tokens went this month
Here’s the tokens distribution according to AgentsView, one of our
Agentic engineering recommendations
to keep tabs on AI usage:
Zooming in on the models split specifically:
The goal was to spend the whole month on GLM 5.3 Flash pictured in teal. Here’s what went well:
Successfully spent the first half of the month on just that model.
That model’s usage was well within our budget ($68, about 4kWh of energy use / 365 grams of carbon emissions).
The second half of the month didn’t go so well, with 1B tokens going to other models.
Unexpected hurdles
The cost of vibe coding
We’re pretty transparent that our
experimental Wagtail MCP server is a vibe-coded prototype
. Vibe coding isn’t quite what we normally aspire to, but for a prototype it’s spot on. Unfortunately there are still consequences to it. I chose the 'wrong' model for the prototype, and we spent 450M tokens / $150 / 5kWh of energy use almost overnight. The MCP server itself works well and we now have a great demo of the capabilities, so it’s not for nothing:
Nonetheless, it’s a good reminder to be careful with model selection and with agentic patterns. We could have achieved similar results for most likely 5x less cost with not that much more effort. Lessons learned! We need to budget for this, and be more careful. Could have seen it coming, but now we know.
Infrastructure woes
Another unexpected hurdle was infrastructure availability issues. We’ve written extensively about
comparing inference providers
. Our choices work really most of the times, but it turns out they’re very popular, and do not have the same capacity as the big labs who hoard all the GPUs. We noted degradation with the performance of GLM 5.3 Flash in particular, most likely because of it being
so high up
the Pareto frontier of relevant models for our work.
This meant having to switch to other similar models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash). Which is very simple to do, but nonetheless unexpected!
The cost of experimentation and R&D
Last but not least, beyond using one model for day-to-day engineering, it felt essential to keep experimenting with a wide range of models, keeping up with what providers are releasing. This is particularly essential as we start to benchmark models’ performance on Wagtail tasks, where we need data across a wide range of models. Sneak peek of our benchmark:
It’s much easier to guide people towards leaner options with this kind of concrete data. And for us to make those options even more viable with agent skills, or
our new CLI prototype
, which is intended to work well with agents.
Takeways and what to do next
So technically this challenge was a failure. Only 50% usage on the target model, 1B out of 2B tokens. About 35 kWh of energy use instead of 10. But we did learn a lot, which is crucial for the current moment. Reflecting on this for October, here’s what will make it work:
Constant, local usage measurement and reporting
. Looking not just at tokens but also energy use and spend, and ideally how well this all leads to concrete positive outcomes.
Budgeting for experimentation, not just day-to-day tasks
. Making more concerted decisions about which prototypes are worth building, and how.
Better prompt selection and multi-agent techniques
. Orchestrator vs. scout vs. implementer vs. reviewer agents. Bounded goals. Not rocket science but certainly one more thing to learn.
Keep pushing for more efficient techniques and models
. The Jev-style decision diffusion models look very promising if they can run so efficiently. Latest flagship models also look like a step in the right direction on that front.
For day-to-day developer work, it’s totally viable to focus on one or two flash-tier cheap models. A viable target is probably that the
majority
of AI inference work should be done with such efficient models, measured in cost or energy use rather than meaningless tokens. That’s the goal for October! You should try it too, you’ll learn a lot in the process.
And come say hi at
Wagtail Space 2026
in November to hear how that all pans out!

• **成本与预算观点**：一个月代理式编码仅约68美元，说明模型选择已同时是质量和预算决策；但原型因选错模型一夜消耗4.5亿token、150美元，理论上可用约五分之一成本完成，凸显需预估token消耗并谨慎设计agent流程。  
• **评测方法质疑**：只比较“每token成本”不够，还应考察完成任务所需token数、速度，以及每项任务的实际成本和耗时。  
• **原型开发观点**：AI适合快速试错和复杂原型，但首版往往应被丢弃，不宜直接用于高风险生产系统。

补充讨论：有人惊讶4kWh能耗极低，并据此推测AI数据中心建设可能过度扩张；也有人怀疑高额消耗与缓存失效或未补贴的推理服务有关。

data.title: Show HN: Giving Opus 5.5 a simulated paint canvas
data.author: alstonite
data.article_summary: 文章介绍一个让AI模型“绘画”的项目：模型不生成图像，而是编写程序，在模拟油画颜料、画布和画笔的虚拟画架上逐笔作画。75幅作品多以弗里德里希等艺术家为主题，也有自由创作。项目发现不同模型常重复选择海岸、黄昏、裸体树、陶罐和柠檬等意象，甚至在未互相参照时创作出近似画面，并通过多轮作画、观看和评审比较其表现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM通过代码和视觉反馈自主绘画的能力、创作过程及其对艺术的影响。

不同观点：
• 惊叹与乐观：模型能自然推进绘画，效果可能相当于人类数周工作；业余画家可借此低成本试验新技法、避免毁掉画布，并加速像素画等创作。
• 质疑作品质量：画面虽“惊艳”却有违和感，例如风景中密集教堂不合逻辑；模型仍不擅长手部，偶尔因错误的厚涂、笔刷纹理把作品彻底毁掉。
• 过程导向：相比直接生成成品，更值得研究的是让AI执行“创作过程”、自行编写工具；有人主张成果应保留源代码或项目文件，便于人类检查、学习和复现。
• AI是否是艺术家：部分评论认为AI本质仍是工具，人类仍会借新工具创作；也有人担忧商业艺术很快大量AI化，削弱艺术中人与人的连接并冲击艺术家生计。
• 技术机制与透明度：模型似乎能调用“look”工具观察画布，且会关注后台评测器，甚至可能为评分优化；评论者希望了解具体作者采用的技术，以及像Opus这类文本模型如何完成绘画。

补充讨论：讨论还提到相关先例（“Training AI to Paint with Code”、Pindar Van Arman），并以“Claude Monet”双关命名提出趣味建议。

data.title: Woking Electrical Control Room (2016)
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了英国沃金电力控制室的历史与内部设施。该建筑建于1936年，由瑞典公司建造、建筑师James Robb Scott设计，是南部铁路电网五座控制室之一。控制室通过控制面板管理沿线变电站，工程师可迅速调整电力供应、处理故障。其独特的椭圆形大厅、穹顶、铜制灯具和铸铁柱极具特色。1997年停止主要使用，现为二级保护建筑，每年仅少量开放参观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：老式控制室的功能设计、视觉美感、历史保存价值，以及其与现代数字化基础设施的对比。

不同观点：
• [xg15]认为旧式控制室不仅显示系统状态，还直观呈现线路、管道和组件结构，像一张可操作的地图；现代软件仪表盘多是复杂指标图表，却常缺乏系统整体结构。
• [SoftTalker、adonovan]起初以为控制室仍在运行，后确认已于1997年停用；他们惊叹于经济萧条时期基础设施仍重视美学，如今类似场所可能只剩屏幕、地毯和标准化办公设施。
• [footydude]赞赏“功能性与适度庄严感”的结合，认为1930—1970年代工业设施正逐渐成为具有魅力的历史空间，并思考未来人们会如何看待当代基础设施。
• [MadnessASAP]怀念实体开关、指示灯带来的触觉和责任感，认为云计算削弱了人对基础设施的直观感受；[intrasight]则强调许多技术空间和实物缺乏影像记录。
• [tolerance]指出这类环境的吸引力几乎与“临界空间”审美相反；[actinium226]认为其充满电子游戏场景般的魅力。

补充讨论：控制室已被历史保存，并作为影视拍摄场地出租；评论还分享了实景照片链接，并提到相关网站字体难读。

49938399.article_content:
Menu
Woking Electrical Control Room: UK September 2016
The Woking control room was built during 1936. One of five control rooms built to control the electricity on the Southern Rail network. A Swedish firm Asean was contracted to construct the flat roof building which was designed by architect James Robb Scott.
Externally a fairly non descript concrete block with some windows houses one of the finest control rooms I have seen. A large oval room with white domed ceiling houses a small central switchboard desk and four decorative cast iron poles each holding up a large copper dish, these light up the room with huge bulbs which resemble a small rugby ball. Other than these five items the room is pretty much empty, however the walls are adorned with black control panels.
As you can see each separate panel is related to a certain location. These panels control the substation at each location, I believe mercury arc rectifiers were spread out evenly along the line also. If faults were reported they could perform rapid reconfiguration of the electricity flow with the panels so there was no actual downtime on the railways.
It only took two on site engineers to control this section of the railway and organise repair work when faults occurred.  Ironically with controlling all this electricity they still had to wind up the switchboard to use the telephone.
The control room remained in use up until 1997 when a new substation further down the line took over most of the tasks. Only one other of the five control rooms survive, sadly this has been stripped out and is used for storage.
The offices here are still in constant use and the building is grade ii listed. It does open for one or two days a year as part of the Open London heritage weekend which is how I got the pleasure to visit this awesome delight.

data.title: C++ Insights – See your source code with the eyes of a Compiler
data.author: rramadass
data.article_summary: C++ Insights 是一个基于 Clang 的 C++ 源码转换工具，旨在以接近开发者熟悉的 C++ 形式展示编译器在幕后完成的工作。它可展开编译器隐式生成的特殊成员函数，揭示类型推导、运算符调用、类型转换，以及 Lambda、范围 for 循环、结构化绑定等语法糖的实际实现。项目支持在线使用和本地构建，仍在持续完善对新标准的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 C++ Insights 这类工具如何展示 C++ 编译器对源代码的转换、其教育价值，以及 C++ 语言复杂性和工具改进方向展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **工具有助于理解编译器行为**：jsrcout 认为它能回答“编译器到底在想什么”；IshKebab 表示该工具帮助自己理解 Lambda；StilesCrisis 希望示例加入 Lambda 捕获，以展示更多“编译器魔法”。
• **工具可用于教学和可视化执行过程**：alankarmisra 分享了类似的 C++→Clang→JavaScript 转译器，可在网页中展示变量状态变化、逐步执行，并支持修改输入后重新计算。
• **关注转译代码的正确性**：veexx103 提出从 Clang AST 重构出的代码存在无法编译等问题，询问这些问题能否解决，反映出工具在代码生成完整性和实用性上的挑战。
• **希望扩展到编译性能分析**：kvemkon 建议进一步显示每个代码块（尽可能细粒度）的编译耗时。
• **对 C++ 复杂性的反思与批评**：f1shy 虽认可工具价值，却认为语言本身过于复杂、语义不够直观，甚至需要“像律师一样”理解；他主张编程语言应更像数学，帮助人形式化思考，而非让人困惑。
• **存在类似或竞争方案**：tweedler290 提到语言无关的 Benzi，支持另外九种语言，认为其方案覆盖面更广，但承认本工具可能对 C++ 研究更深入。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：该工具是优秀的学习与调试辅助，还是从侧面暴露了 C++ 语言设计过度复杂的问题。

What
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source
transformation. The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes.
It's about the magic the compiler does for us to make things work.
Take this piece of code, for example:
class
Base
{
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
};
int
main
() {
Derived d;
Derived d2 = d;
d2 = d;
Base& b = d;
}
Nothing special, and of course, it compiles. This is the compiler's view on it:
class
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Base() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base(const Base &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base & operator=(const Base &) noexcept = default;
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Derived() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived & operator=(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
};
int
main
()
{
Derived d;
Derived d2 =
Derived
(d);
d2.
operator
=(d);
Base & b =
static_cast
<Base&>(d);
return
0
;
}
You can see all the compiler-provided special member functions and the upcast from
Derived
to
Base
.
Why
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source transformation.
The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes. It's about the magic the compiler does
for us to make things work. Or looking through the classes of a compiler.
In 2017, I started looking into some new things we got with C++11, C++14, and C++17. Amazing things like lambdas, range-based for-loops,
and structured bindings. I put it together in a talk. You can find the
slides
and a
video
online.
However, all that research and some of my training and teaching got me to start thinking about how it would be if we could see with the eyes
of the compiler. Sure, there is an AST dump, at least for Clang. We can see what code the compiler generates from a C++ source snippet with
tools like Compiler Explorer. However, what we see is assembler. Neither the AST nor the Compiler Explorer output is in the language I write
code. Hence, I'm not very familiar with this output. Plus, when teaching students C++, showing an AST and explaining that it is all there was
not quite satisfying for me.
I started to write a Clang-based tool that can transform a range-based for-loop into the compiler-internal version. Then, I did the same
for structured bindings and lambdas. In the end, I did much more than initially planned. It shows where operators are
invoked and places in which the compiler does some casting. C++ Insights can deduce the type behind
auto
or
decltype
. The goal
is to produce compilable code. However, this is not possible in all places.
You can see, for example, the transformation of a
lambda
,
range-based for-loop
, or
auto
. Of course, you can transform any other C++ snippet.
See yourself. C++ Insights is available online:
cppinsights.io
.
Still, there is work to do.
I do not claim to get all the things right. I'm also working on supporting features from new standards, like C++20, at the moment.

49928361.article_summary: C++ Insights 是一个基于 Clang 的 C++ 源码转换工具，旨在以接近开发者熟悉的 C++ 形式展示编译器在幕后完成的工作。它可展开编译器隐式生成的特殊成员函数，揭示类型推导、运算符调用、类型转换，以及 Lambda、范围 for 循环、结构化绑定等语法糖的实际实现。项目支持在线使用和本地构建，仍在持续完善对新标准的支持。
49928361.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 C++ Insights 这类工具如何展示 C++ 编译器对源代码的转换、其教育价值，以及 C++ 语言复杂性和工具改进方向展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **工具有助于理解编译器行为**：jsrcout 认为它能回答“编译器到底在想什么”；IshKebab 表示该工具帮助自己理解 Lambda；StilesCrisis 希望示例加入 Lambda 捕获，以展示更多“编译器魔法”。
• **工具可用于教学和可视化执行过程**：alankarmisra 分享了类似的 C++→Clang→JavaScript 转译器，可在网页中展示变量状态变化、逐步执行，并支持修改输入后重新计算。
• **关注转译代码的正确性**：veexx103 提出从 Clang AST 重构出的代码存在无法编译等问题，询问这些问题能否解决，反映出工具在代码生成完整性和实用性上的挑战。
• **希望扩展到编译性能分析**：kvemkon 建议进一步显示每个代码块（尽可能细粒度）的编译耗时。
• **对 C++ 复杂性的反思与批评**：f1shy 虽认可工具价值，却认为语言本身过于复杂、语义不够直观，甚至需要“像律师一样”理解；他主张编程语言应更像数学，帮助人形式化思考，而非让人困惑。
• **存在类似或竞争方案**：tweedler290 提到语言无关的 Benzi，支持另外九种语言，认为其方案覆盖面更广，但承认本工具可能对 C++ 研究更深入。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：该工具是优秀的学习与调试辅助，还是从侧面暴露了 C++ 语言设计过度复杂的问题。

On the escalation of war in Ethiopia
The coming proxy wars will be devastating for civilians and do little to improve governance and human welfare in Ethiopia and the wider Horn
Ken Opalo
Oct 01, 2026
67
7
19
Share
Thank you for being a regular reader of
An Africanist Perspective
. If you haven’t done so yet, please hit subscribe to receive timely updates on new posts along with over 36,000 other subscribers. New regular content is free. Book reviews and the archives are gated.
Subscribe
I: On Ethiopia’s wars of choice, motivated by historical grievances and elite hubris
Source:
Wikipedia
This is from the ICG:
Northern Ethiopia is slipping into renewed war. After months of building tensions, on 23 September large-scale hostilities broke out between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and Amhara Fano militias, on one side, and the federal government and allied Tigrayan forces on the other. Responsibility for the escalation lies primarily with the TPLF, which launched ground assaults in coordination with other rebels with whom it has joined hands in a new alliance that vows to overthrow Ethiopia’s government. The upsurge in fighting comes almost five months after the TPLF retook power in the Tigray region, dealing a blow to a 2022 peace deal that had ended the last Tigray war and leading Addis Ababa to mount an intensifying drone campaign against TPLF forces.
I maintain that war in Ethiopia (and the wider Horn) is not inevitable
. The current outbreak of war reflects the fact that Ethiopian elites keep choosing war over peace. Unfortunately, despite repeatedly choosing war, Ethiopian leaders continue to enjoy support from a cast of warmongering academics, journalists, public intellectuals, civil society actors, and a whole host of foreign actors — all of whom have long taken sides and become cheerleaders for their respective camps.
Let’s be blunt. There are a lot of things not to like about the Abiy Ahmed administration. The strong elements of autocratic intolerance, often expressed in the form of indiscriminate force. The unwillingness to (publicly) countenance alternative worldviews and policy positions. The abiding reliance on the old vindictive governance styles anchored around identity politics and collective punishment. And the hubristic promotion of a personality cult, which makes it difficult to build the broad and durable coalitions needed to govern a diverse country like Ethiopia.
Perhaps the political situation would be marginally better if Prime Minister Abiy were a better politician.
However, I doubt it. To understand why, it’s worth stepping back to appreciate the
structural drivers of elite instability and conflict in Ethiopia
:
The last three decades in Ethiopia have been a search for a new myth. The ethno-federalist system had legitimate logic: bringing about the dignity of (cultural and linguistic) difference between nations and nationalities. However, its rhetoric was drawn from the difficult past instead of the hope of better future. To make matters worse, it became a breeding ground for social and economic injustice.
In the absence of farsighted political elites who may have been able to craft a new inclusive myth out of the stories of nations and nationalities, ethnic groups had to walk back to find their stories in their own small compartments. This exacerbated narrow ethnic histories and ideals.
It’s easy to demonize Abiy. But the hard truth is that
Ethiopia’s structural problems preceded him
and, if left unresolved, will outlast him.
Those beating the war drums the loudest in Ethiopia — and who’ve trashed the Pretoria Agreement — are convinced that Ethiopia can only be well governed if they are in charge. Nearly all are motivated by maximalist demands and are quick to weaponize legitimate historical grievances for parochial ends. The leading characters involved are (mostly) men out to settle decades-old scores and who prefer to go out fighting rather than accept political defeat by their perceived inferiors. These same characters have been able to mobilize fighters under the banner of uncompromising primordislist ethno-nationalism and commitments to their respective ethno-states.
Subscribe
In light of all this,
Teklehaymanot G. Weldemichel
is spot in making the case for following through on the Pretoria Agreement. Yes, it is imperfect and the various belligerents haven’t always followed through on the deal’s requirements. However, the deal “
brought large-scale fighting to an end and contains commitments that address some key unresolved issues
.” It’s a start. It ought to be given a chance.
Unfortunately, the plight of civilians hardly ever features in the calculus of the warmongers. Estimate vary, but the death toll in the Tigray war may have been as high as a staggering 600,000. This is a monumentally catastrophic figure. Even the lower bound estimates out there would make it one of the deadliest wars of the 21st century. Given what we know about how belligerents go about wa

data.title: Show HN: Germany's new sovereign AI model Kolibri
data.author: tejaskumar__
data.article_summary: Kolibri是Aleph Alpha于2026年10月发布的德英双语开源大模型，采用78.1B参数混合专家架构，每个token仅激活约34.6亿参数。模型支持超长上下文、推理和工具调用，以Apache 2.0许可发布，主要在德国、芬兰训练，强调符合欧盟法规、数据主权和本地部署。文章介绍其架构、德语优化、优势、局限及运行场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Aleph Alpha 的 Kolibri 主权 AI 模型，评论集中于其实际能力、评测公平性、技术定位及“主权 AI”的价值。

不同观点：
• **主权与审计价值**：有人认为主权模型最重要的用途不是全面领先，而是审计其他模型的工具调用和最终结果，作为政府应用中的“信任适配器”；若成本和速度足够低，具备商业价值。  
• **技术表现认可**：部分用户在 RTX Pro 6000 上测试后认为其速度很快（FP8 约170 token/s、仅3B激活参数），也有人对实际效果感到意外，认为开源权重和公共产品属性值得肯定。  
• **能力与产品定位质疑**：批评者指出它记忆知识较少、多轮工具调用较弱、编码代理能力不突出，并且“过度思考”、消耗过多 token，因此质疑其核心优势。  
• **评测与参数比较争议**：评论质疑为何未与更新的 Qwen3.8 Flash 对比，却选择近一年前的 Qwen3-Next；同时争论“27B dense 比 78B MoE 更大”的说法，焦点在总参数与激活参数不能简单等同。  
• **公司与项目评价分化**：有人认为 Aleph Alpha 已落后、人才流失、项目交付不佳；也有人将其视为德国及欧洲在主权 AI 上比英国更积极的尝试。

补充讨论：多人认为该帖子只是博客宣传，不符合“Show HN”主题；另有讽刺其“德语思考”意味着守时、爱用缩写和凡事成立委员会，并质疑官网缺少德语选项。

49943034.article_content:
Kolibri is an open-weight large language model (LLM) from
Aleph Alpha
for German and English: a mixture of experts with 78 billion parameters that only uses about 3.5 billion of them for each token it reads or writes.
It came out on 3 October 2026 under the
Apache 2.0 license
, the weights are
on Hugging Face
, and it was trained from scratch on infrastructure in Germany and Finland. (Kolibri is German for hummingbird, which is cute for a model whose whole trick is being light.)
I live in Germany, and at
SmashingConf New York
in 2024 I told the room what I’d heard in the US when I said where I’m based: “you regulate, you don’t innovate.” It hurt to hear, and what I wished for on that stage was the middle, “the right balance between innovation and regulation around data privacy, data stewardship, environmental constraints and energy requirements.” Kolibri is a pretty direct answer to that: a German team built it with the
EU AI Act
in mind “from the ground up”, and in Aleph Alpha’s own evaluation it scores above every compared model of its size in both languages.
Huge congrats to everyone at Aleph Alpha who built it, my good friend
Michael Hofmann
among them!
This post is about how Kolibri works, where it’s strong, where it isn’t, how to run it, and when it’s the right pick. Everything here comes from Aleph Alpha’s
189 page technical report
,
the model card
and
their launch post
, plus one experiment I ran on its tokenizer.
What is Kolibri?
Kolibri 1
Parameters
78.1 billion in total, 3.46 billion per token (4.4%)
Languages
German and English
Context
262,144 tokens natively, tested up to 1,048,576
License
Apache 2.0 for the weights and configuration files (Aleph Alpha keeps the rights to its training code and methods)
Memory
about 78 GB of weights in 8-bit floating point (FP8)
Reasoning
4 levels: none, low, medium and high
Tool calling
Yes
Knowledge cutoff
18 June 2026
Training
about 24 trillion tokens, more than a fifth of them German, on 768
NVIDIA B200
graphics processing units (GPUs)
Aleph Alpha calls Kolibri sovereign, and in their launch post that means 2 things.
The first is how it was built: “teams built the model in Germany, trained it on infrastructure in Germany and Finland, under European and German law, with no foreign control.” The second is what customers get: “full freedom of deployment and intellectual-property safety, so compliance comes as an inherited property.” In plain words, a ministry or a car supplier can run it on its own servers, with its data never leaving the building, and nobody can change or switch off the model under them. Aleph Alpha has also signed the
European Union
’s
General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Code of Practice
.
Sovereign doesn’t mean that nothing from outside Europe went in, and the model card says so itself: English web text was rephrased with Google’s
Gemma 4
, German with
Mistral-NeMo
, and
Qwen3-32B
labeled data for the quality filters. They then filtered the training data for the political bias such models can have, which they’ve
measured in Chinese open models
themselves.
How Kolibri works
Kolibri is 6 ideas stacked on top of each other, and each one is there to make German cheaper, longer or more honest.
1. 384 specialists, and each token sees 6
In a normal (dense) model, every token goes through every parameter. In a
mixture of experts (MoE)
, each layer has a crowd of small sub-networks called experts and a router that picks a few of them for each token. Kolibri has 50 layers, each with 384 experts plus 1 shared expert that every token goes through, and its router sends each token to 6 of the 384. That’s how 78.1 billion parameters turn into 3.46 billion of actual work per token.
In 2024 I gave a talk called
Why Small Language Models are the future
, and I argued for “smaller language models with fewer parameters and fewer places things can go wrong that require lesser compute.” My analogy was a doctor who has read every medical book in the world against a specialist in hematology: go to the first one with a blood condition and “they may not get it right cuz they know too much.” A mixture of experts puts a hospital full of specialists inside one model, and the router is the receptionist who sends each token to the right 6.
The analogy breaks in 2 places though. The experts aren’t neat topics like “German law”: when researchers
look inside MoE models
they mostly find experts for patterns of tokens, like punctuation or proper nouns, not subjects a person would pick. And the hospital has to keep all 384 specialists on staff even if you only see 6, so
Kolibri computes like a 3.5 billion parameter model but needs the memory of a 78 billion parameter one.
The model card says it plainly: “the full model must be held in memory even though only part of it is active at any time.”
2. A tokenizer that reads long German words
A model doesn’t read letters or words, it reads tokens: chunks of text from a fixed vocabulary, picked when the tokenizer is trained. German glues words t

• **评测与参数比较争议**：评论质疑为何未与更新的 Qwen3.8 Flash 对比，却选择近一年前的 Qwen3-Next；同时争论“27B dense 比 78B MoE 更大”的说法，焦点在总参数与激活参数不能简单等同。  
• **公司与项目评价分化**：有人认为 Aleph Alpha 已落后、人才流失、项目交付不佳；也有人将其视为德国及欧洲在主权 AI 上比英国更积极的尝试。

补充讨论：多人认为该帖子只是博客宣传，不符合“Show HN”主题；另有讽刺其“德语思考”意味着守时、爱用缩写和凡事成立委员会，并质疑官网缺少德语选项。

data.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
data.author: bastitx
data.article_summary: Aleph Alpha发布Kolibri主权开放权重模型，采用英德混合专家架构，总参数780亿、激活参数30亿，支持最长100万Token上下文，并以Apache 2.0开源。模型专注德语、推理、数学、代理及政务、工业、航空航天等关键领域，支持本地部署，强调供应链透明、数据与知识产权安全。其性能、成本和吞吐表现优异，部分任务可媲美激活参数规模大数倍的模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Aleph Alpha 发布 Kolibri 模型的开放性、性能、主权定位及实际可靠性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **高度肯定开放透明**：评论认为论文像完整教程，详细公开训练方法和数据集，体现少见的透明度；团队年轻、迭代快，且模型在编程和智能体任务上表现不错。  
• **支持可用性与抗幻觉设计**：Kolibri 通过 abstention data 和 Merlin-Arthur 协议训练，能够在缺乏上下文时回答“不知道”；有人因此提供 Kolibri-1 免费体验。  
• **性能与评测存疑**：有人指出 Qwen3.8 27B 在其德语基准中以79.9分超过 Kolibri 的70.8分；评测避开了更新的 Qwen3.8 Flash，却选择近一年前的模型比较，可能不够公平。  
• **主权定位存在争议**：Aleph Alpha 若并入加拿大 Cohere，且主要由多伦多运营和持有，“德国主权 AI”说法是否成立受到质疑；也有人认为非美、非中企业应通过跨国合作分摊成本。  
• **模型能力与实用性不足**：有人体验到模型“过度思考”、耗费过多 token；德语和英语双语定位被认为限制了数据规模与知识覆盖。实际咨询德国网站法律声明时，模型引用已废止的 Telemediengesetz，未主动使用现行 DDG，暴露出时效性和可靠性问题。  
• **主权应扩展至完整技术栈**：讨论认为仅能自托管模型还不够，嵌入、检索、记忆和工具调用也需自主可控；主权模型还可作为其他模型的“信任适配器”进行结果审计。

补充讨论：FP16 版本难以在普通 Mac 上运行；有人对其用于航空航天等高风险场景表示谨慎。

49942706.article_content:
Research
Aleph Alpha
03/10/2026
Kolibri Has Landed: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
On the Day of German Reunification, we are releasing our new model: Kolibri.
Kolibri is an English-German Mixture-of-Experts Transformer with 78B total parameters, 3B
active. It supports context lengths of up to 1M tokens. The model can be downloaded with the
full weights on
Hugging Face
and used under the Apache 2.0 license terms.
Kolibri is the result of continuous iteration of our model training effort. We first built
a model training pipeline
and validated it by building Kolibri Origin, a 30B total, 3B active model with a much shorter
65k token context window. Kolibri ran through the same pipeline: from data ingestion and curation,
through ablations, pre-training, and post-training, to the final evals. It enabled running hundreds
of ablation experiments and stable pre-training that ran without a person having to step in when
hardware failed or a data connection dropped. We continuously monitored training metrics and standardized
monitoring for custom benchmarks. The time we put into building and iterating on this pipeline
was a valuable investment. We see it in how much better Kolibri is than Kolibri Origin, and in
how little time separates their releases.
Kolibri is a specialized language model built for sovereign mission-critical work in
regulated areas including public administration, industrials and aerospace. We specialized
Kolibri for German, reasoning, math, agentic behavior, and further capabilities our
customers need in production. The aim of this specialization was to optimize performance in
our customers' specific use cases. Through specialization, customers achieve contextualized
performance in their AI operations and they can monitor its economic impact, so that ROI
stays measurable and grows over time.
Specialization alone is not enough. Sovereignty is just as important. Sovereignty, for us,
combines two dimensions: how we built the model, and how it transfers to our customers. We
offer full supply-chain integrity and account for every decision, from data ingestion,
through pre- and post-training, to the final evaluations. We provide transparency. Customers
have full freedom of deployment and intellectual-property safety, so compliance comes as an
inherited property of the model.
Read our
tech report
for full details.
What Kolibri Delivers
We optimized Kolibri for performance across a wide range of sectors considering their
particular domain-specific language, regulatory, and procedural realities. Its small and
efficient size provides our customers with flexibility to run it efficiently on-premise,
without sending internal data to third-party inference services. The spotlight in this
section introduces the model's capabilities, before we describe them in section
How we built Kolibri at high velocity
.
Foundational capabilities for enterprise and government
With Kolibri we optimize the trade-off between model capability and deployment costs, using
3B active parameters out of 78B total. Kolibri sits on the Pareto frontier for quality
versus serving cost, for both English and German. The Pareto frontier is a concept from
economics, marking the best achievable combinations of two objectives, where improving on
one means giving up some of the other. None of the compared models delivers more quality at
the same serving cost, or the same quality at lower cost.

Research, design, and product teams at ServiceNow, Brex and Canva run their customer research on us, and we raised a $13M Series A led by Inovia late last year after going through YC in 2021.

Product Engineer here means you take a problem and run with it end to end - from the customer conversation to production to validating whether it actually worked. From there you're trusted to find the right solution, because you're close to the customer and you have great product sense. You'll build across the product stack - from Rails APIs and React/TypeScript frontends to video streaming, realtime voice agents, agentic search, product analytics, and everything in between - working directly with the founders, our designer, and the rest of engineering.

data.title: Show HN: Offrun – manage every coding agent from one workspace
data.author: arunbhatia
data.article_summary: Offrun是一款Mac端多智能体编程工具，可直接运行Claude Code、Codex等CLI，无需新账号或API密钥。它为每个代理创建独立Git worktree，支持并行开发、代码审查、账户切换与额度接续，并提供项目记忆、通知和结果预览，帮助用户安全高效管理代理任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该产品与现有 AI Agent/账户管理工具的差异化，以及平台支持、功能和实际使用价值。

不同观点：
• **产品并不新颖**：已有 Goose、Paseo、T3 Code 等类似产品，因此需要明确自身创新点。  
• **与 Paseo 等产品相比缺乏优势**：用户认为 Paseo 功能更完整，支持通过 Tailscale 和移动端远程连接其他机器上的 LLM Agent，体验也较好。  
• **平台兼容性受到质疑**：目前似乎仅支持 Apple Silicon Mac，不支持 Linux、Windows 或 Intel Mac，限制了目标用户范围。  
• **应与 Herdr 正面比较**：评论指出 Herdr 支持更多平台且已融资 600 万美元，产品方需要解释相较 Herdr 的核心差异和竞争力。  
• **自定义能力是关键问题**：潜在用户关心能否接入自己的 Agent harness，以及产品提供的能力是否超过用户自行“vibe code”实现的功能。  
• **需要提供任务前的账户额度信息**：用户希望在派发任务前看到各账户的速率限制剩余空间，而不是任务进行中才发现额度不足。

补充讨论：有人因文案“and what every account has left”而联想到 LLM 生成，暗示产品介绍的措辞可能不够自然。整体争议焦点是：产品是否真正具备独特价值，还是仅重复已有工具的功能。

主要讨论点：该产品与现有 AI Agent/账户管理工具的差异化，以及平台支持、功能和实际使用价值。

不同观点：
• **产品并不新颖**：已有 Goose、Paseo、T3 Code 等类似产品，因此需要明确自身创新点。  
• **与 Paseo 等产品相比缺乏优势**：用户认为 Paseo 功能更完整，支持通过 Tailscale 和移动端远程连接其他机器上的 LLM Agent，体验也较好。  
• **平台兼容性受到质疑**：目前似乎仅支持 Apple Silicon Mac，不支持 Linux、Windows 或 Intel Mac，限制了目标用户范围。  
• **应与 Herdr 正面比较**：评论指出 Herdr 支持更多平台且已融资 600 万美元，产品方需要解释相较 Herdr 的核心差异和竞争力。  
• **自定义能力是关键问题**：潜在用户关心能否接入自己的 Agent harness，以及产品提供的能力是否超过用户自行“vibe code”实现的功能。  
• **需要提供任务前的账户额度信息**：用户希望在派发任务前看到各账户的速率限制剩余空间，而不是任务进行中才发现额度不足。

补充讨论：有人因文案“and what every account has left”而联想到 LLM 生成，暗示产品介绍的措辞可能不够自然。整体争议焦点是：产品是否真正具备独特价值，还是仅重复已有工具的功能。

data.title: An Update on Orion for Linux and Windows
data.author: pentagrama
data.article_summary: Kagi宣布停止开发Orion的Linux和Windows版本，并将两者开源，供社区接手维护。由于团队规模小，公司将集中资源提升macOS和iOS版的速度、稳定性与功能。Linux测试版仍可使用，但2026年10月2日后不再获官方更新；Windows版原定于2026年发布，今后将由社区推动。Kagi还将寻求开源组织参与长期维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kagi停止或缩减Orion浏览器多平台开发，围绕其定位、开源前景、产品取舍及Kagi战略方向展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持收缩或停止：Orion定位不清，Firefox、Brave等已提供隐私功能；专有软件在Linux上缺乏吸引力，且跨平台维护成本高。部分用户认为Mac版也应取消，转而投入Zen等更有影响力的浏览器。
• 支持开源延续：有人欢迎将Orion开源，认为浏览器市场仍需要多样性，社区或许能继续Linux/AOSP等平台开发；理想方案是开源、拥有类似Arc的界面并修复现有问题。
• 质疑产品质量：iOS版存在性能差、交互控件失效等问题，体验明显不如Safari；缺少Linux版本也使部分Kagi用户直接放弃使用。
• 主张回归搜索：一些订阅者认为Kagi应专注搜索服务，浏览器、翻译等业务可能导致资源分散；有人已因搜索失败、服务可靠性下降而重新考虑续费。
• 仍看好战略价值：支持者认为Orion可与Kagi搜索、Assistant及未来AI/代理功能整合，浏览器能提供隐私保护和产品差异化。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于Orion究竟是Kagi生态的战略入口，还是偏离搜索核心的负担；同时，用户对Kagi频繁扩张、转向美国市场及后续是否会彻底关闭Orion存在担忧。

49941447.article_content:
All Posts
Copy link
Today we have an important update.
We are ending development of Orion for Linux and Windows, and we're open-sourcing both so the community can carry them forward.
Kagi is stepping back from developing these platforms directly so our team can put more focus on
Orion for macOS and iOS
.
Orion is built by a very small team, just a handful of developers, funded entirely by Kagi users. We also chose to build it the hard way by not forking Chromium. That independence matters more than ever. The web needs more than one engine, and more than one company deciding what a browser should be.
When we announced Orion for Linux, the response was overwhelming. Many of you were thrilled, tested early builds, filed bug reports, and told us how much you wanted a WebKit-based browser on Linux that respects your privacy. Thank you. That work will soon belong to everyone.
Why we're doing this
When we decided to take Orion beyond the Apple ecosystem, we knew it was a big bet for a small, independent company. We made it because we believe owning the whole experience beginning with the browser, matters.
Building a cross-platform browser is something usually done by companies backed by venture capital or by large open-source communities. Kagi is neither. One thing we hear often from members is that they want us focused. They're right. Rather than spread a small team across three platforms, we're putting our energy where we can do our best work and opening the rest to people who want to take it further.
What this means for Orion on macOS and iOS
Orion for macOS and iOS isn't changing, except to get better. The team and resources that were split across platforms are now focused on making Orion on Apple devices faster, more stable, and more capable. Expect steady improvements in the coming months.
Download Orion for macOS
Download Orion for iOS
What open-sourcing looks like
We'll release the source code for Orion for Linux and Orion for Windows. A lot of good work went into it, and it deserves a future even if we aren't the ones who finish it now. We're thinking about this carefully and will release details in the next 30 days.
We've also reached out to open-source foundations and organizations about long-term stewardship. To be clear about our role: Kagi won't be the core maintainer. These projects need people who want to own them.
Get involved
If you're a developer, maintainer, or organization interested in stewarding Orion for Linux or Windows, we want to hear from you. Reach us at
support@kagi.com
.
What this means for current users
Linux:
The current Linux Beta will keep working, but it will stop receiving updates from Kagi after
October 2, 2026
. We don't recommend using it as your main browser.
Windows:
We had planned to launch Orion for Windows in late 2026. That release won't come from Kagi. Instead, the code will be available for the community to build on. If you signed up for the Windows newsletter, this will be the last update you receive from that list.
Thank you
To everyone who tested, reported bugs, and believed in an independent browser beyond the Apple ecosystem: thank you. You helped build something worth sharing, and we're glad to share it with the community.
Thank you for your patience, your enthusiasm, and your trust.
â the Kagi team

49917536.article_content:
what is going on with ceiling fans
Sep 29, 2026
4,661 notes
Sometimes new design phenomena slip past even those of us who are most in tune with the happenings of the built environment. Such is the case with whatever the hell is going on with commercial ceiling fan design. Being a member of the renting class, a ceiling fan is something that is beyond my scope of purchase. All that aside, when I found myself trying to find inspiration for how to update the one in my apartment (which has very hideous lighting elements) what I saw genuinely shook me to my core.
BEHOLD:
“Fandeliers!” “LED Sculptural Lighting Modern Fan!” Big Ass Fans rip-offs prone to decapitating the poor denizens of your living room!“ See them: ceiling mounted light with fan (sure!) Ceiling mounted fan with LED element (sure!). Blades made of plastic, shades made of plastic, bodies made out of metal, wrought iron, and plastic made to look like metal and wrought iron! You name it, it’s there! Chaos, it seems, reigns in fanville.
Of course, like anyone these days, before beginning my analysis of the "fan situation” I had to do my due diligence and ascertain whether these fans are, in fact, AI fans. Confusing and perhaps deceptive depictions of scale tend to point one in that direction. However, while the rooms are certainly AI generated, product reviews (yes, these have been purchased!) tell me that the fans are not! To my astonishment, in the years since the pandemic (who knows how many – as I said, I am late to the phenomenon and most of the products listed are new as of last year) the ceiling fan as a genre of architectural detail has been completely torn asunder and remade.
In some ways, this was inevitable. Even before the widespread development of integrated LED lighting fixtures, the remarkable rise of direct to consumer furniture production a la Wayfair or Amazon that took place more than a decade ago has led to an unfathomable proliferation of products, each of which becomes its own algorithmic nugget against which other products are measured and in whose image they are later modified based on those results. Hence why there are so many fans that appear to be cousins of one another.
While outfits like IKEA revolutionized furniture mass production through creating simple and interchangeable parts thus lowering prices at the production level, Wayfair et al have done the opposite by eliminating the labor of the storefront and instead rely entirely on cheap production overseas and the preexisting logistics networks that effortlessly bring fan atrocities directly to our doors. (One of the middlemen this approach eschews is the marketing guy that tells you, hey, that’s an ugly fan.)
Meanwhile, LED light fixtures – which most of these are – allow for new degrees of design flexibility, much of which are “sculptural” in nature. Without the “problem” of the light bulb to solve, light could be diffused in all matter of tubes, shafts, and curlicues. As with any new development, there are tasteful ways of using it, and there are…not tasteful ways of using it. These fixtures are also revolutionary in that they are extremely cheap in the short run – many of these fans cost under $200 – but expensive in the long rung, as the LEDs usually cannot be replaced, causing the whole apparatus to be thrown away.
These humble materialist paeans however do not explain the sheer insanity (one could say the infanity) of the situation at hand. Hybridizations abound. For example, one can say that there is such thing as a “fandelier” – a chandelier with a fan in it, and its dialectical opponent: a fan with a chandelier attached to it. (Perhaps a chandefan?)
Here we see an archetypal fandelier (Rosdorf Park Presnell Dimmable Crystal Ceiling Fan with LED Lights and Remote Control™ - $169 on Wayfair.) In this example, the blades – a cheap plastic – are retractable, and come up above the chandelier. This is not standard, however. Often the opposite is true – they are embedded in the base of the fixture itself. Meanwhile, a chandefan:
A cousin of the fandelier – and the most common form of Neo-Fan – is the flush mounted ceiling fan.  Imagine if your landlord special circular downlight had a fan in it! Wouldn’t that be so awesome!
As you can tell, the fan in this light is pathetically small – basically only about a foot in diameter. However, I suppose a tiny fan fitted 10 feet above the sweltering user is better than nothing? Who doesn’t love an imitation of a stale and inadequate breeze on a day that is desperate for relief from the sun? Maybe your landlord might even let you have one, if he’s nice?
This brings us to another of the “flush fans” – the “border” fan, i.e. a normal fan that for some reason has a border around it. This is pushing the previous categories to their limits. What is fan and what is light become ever less entangled and yet remain inseparable…
By the way, there is a subset of this fan that can only be described as:

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Newgrounds 的怀旧体验、社区文化、创作与技术传承，以及 Flash 内容的保存展开。

不同观点：
• 怀旧与共同记忆：许多人回忆《Pico’s School》《Fancy Pants Adventures》《Salad Fingers》等游戏、动画和音乐，认为那是“不同的互联网时代”，承载了青春和校园生活。  
• 社区与创作成长：评论者曾在论坛学习编程、制作 Flash 游戏、音乐和动画，甚至参与 Clock Crew；Newgrounds 为业余创作者提供了展示、交流和成长的平台。Tom Fulp 的经历也体现了个人兴趣可能发展成事业。  
• 内容保存的价值：Ruffle 让旧 Flash 游戏重新可玩，使多年以前的作品免于遗失；不少人惊喜地找回自己的作品和音乐。  
• 商业化的对比：有人认为如今 Roblox、Minecraft 等平台仍延续孩子们创作和社交的模式，但相较 Newgrounds 黄金时期更商业化，社区的“灵魂”较难复制。  
• 参与门槛与遗憾：有人因英语不好只能在其他网站接触 Newgrounds 内容；也有人作品曾被“blammed”而消失，体现平台审核和数字保存的不完整。

补充讨论：评论还涉及沉迷电脑是否健康、早期论坛代码交流，以及 Tom Fulp 对大学计算机课程实用性的质疑，形成“实践创作”与“正规教育”之间的有趣对照。

data.title: Cloudflare OHTTP gateway
data.author: est
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出OHTTP Gateway闭测版，并将Privacy Gateway更名为OHTTP Relay。OHTTP通过“中继+网关”两跳架构，将用户身份与请求内容分离，隐藏IP，减轻开发者隐私保护负担。客户可自建网关搭配Cloudflare中继，或使用Cloudflare托管网关搭配第三方中继；其全球边缘网络旨在降低延迟和运维成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare推出付费OHTTP Gateway后，评论集中于其隐私机制、信任边界、商业动机及滥用治理。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为OHTTP能分离身份与请求内容：Relay知道用户IP，Gateway知道请求但看不到身份，双方无法单独还原完整信息；适合更新检查、隐私分析等场景。  
• 质疑者认为这是把数据从网站日志转移到Cloudflare等大型中心化平台，仍需信任中间方；有人担心其具备“中间人”色彩，甚至认为匿名代理或SOCKS5也能实现类似效果。  
• 有人反对付费隐私功能，认为这会削弱普遍提升隐私的激励；也有人宁愿网站直接看到IP，而不是交给Cloudflare、Google、Meta等巨头。  
• 另一派指出，若网站嵌入Google追踪代码，OHTTP并不能阻止追踪；真正重视隐私的网站应减少第三方网络和行为采集，而非依赖Cloudflare。  
• 安全治理方面，评论担心隐藏IP后难以封禁滥用者、追责攻击来源；在AI代理和自动化滥用增多的情况下，隐私与平台防滥用存在冲突。

补充讨论：争议核心是“减少应用服务器掌握用户身份”是否值得转而信任Cloudflare，以及OHTTP究竟是有效的隐私分权，还是新的集中化数据入口。

49941091.article_content:
Today, end users carry too muchÂ of the burden of online privacy. To avoid third-party trackers or targeted ads, users are instructed to use a VPN, disable cookies, or install adblockers. Meanwhile, some app developers end up knowing more about their users than theyâd care to: a typical client-server exchange creates a trail of user data, like the clientâs IP addressÂ or TLS fingerprint. This level of visibility can be a burden.
Thatâs why Cloudflare builds infrastructure that helps developers bake privacy into their apps. Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) is an
IETF standard
Â designed to enable app backends to receive HTTP requests without seeing user IP addresses.
This fall, weâre launching the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway. Customers will be able to enable our new OHTTP Gateway as a paid add-on to their zone and start receiving OHTTP traffic with just a few clicks. Register through
our form
Â to join our waitlist. Read on to learn more.
Expanding our OHTTP product suite
With OHTTP, requests travel through two independently-operated hops: a relay and a gateway. An OHTTP relay blindly forwards encrypted requests in order to hide client identifiers from app servers. An OHTTP gateway performs the cryptographic work of decapsulating encrypted requests and encapsulating responses such that app servers can handle OHTTP requests as if they were plain HTTP. The separation of trust between relay and gateway is critical: it ensures that no single party sees both client identifiers and request contents.
In 2022, we launched an OHTTP relay product,
Privacy Gateway
. Privacy Gateway enables our customers to offer more privacy-preserving experiences to their users. For example, Flo Health uses OHTTP for their appâs
Anonymous Mode
, and Appleâs
Private Cloud Compute
Â uses OHTTP to disassociate AI inference requests from user identities. But customers who are already protecting their servers behind Cloudflare canât also use a Cloudflare-operated relay â they need an OHTTP gateway instead.
With the existing Cloudflare OHTTP Relay, customers must bring their own Gateway to preserve a separation of trust.
In our experience running OHTTP relays, weâve seen how difficult it can be to build and operate a secure, performant OHTTP gateway at scale. Today, weâre launchingÂ the closed beta for our self-serve Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway. Weâre also renaming ourÂ âPrivacy Gatewayâ to âCloudflare OHTTP Relayâ to better distinguish the two products.Â
Now, customers who want an OHTTP architecture with the necessary separation of trust have two options:
Use Cloudflareâs OHTTP Relay (formerly Cloudflare Privacy Gateway) and run your gateway yourself
. This is best if your application servers are hosted off Cloudflare, and youâre able to run your own OHTTP gateway.
Use Cloudflareâs new OHTTP Gateway with a third-party relay
. This is best if your app servers are already behind Cloudflare (on our CDN or Workers, for example), if youâre accepting OHTTP requests from a third party (like Appleâs
LiveCallerID
), or if you want a managed gateway to minimize latency and operational overhead. Â
Weâre working to raise the bar for privacy across the Internet, and we believe that protocols like OHTTP can help â if we make them easy enough to adopt. Itâs always been our goal to expand our OHTTP product suite and make our trusted privacy infrastructure accessible to a broader swath of the Internet.
Why we built the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway
SinceÂ we launched our OHTTP Relay product,Â weâve observed a few things.
First, weâve seen that there's a growing appetite among developers for accessible, usable privacy infrastructure. Developers of privacy-oriented apps want to bake network privacy into their applications by default, but doing so remains harder than it should be. Â
Second, weâve learned that building and operating an OHTTP gateway can be tough for customers. Any proxying architecture introduces some latency because requests must travel an extra hop or two around the Internet. Combine that with the cost to decrypt requests and encrypt responses, and the latency hit of a homegrown OHTTP setup can be significant. Weâre well-positioned to solve this problem: the same building blocks that enable us to operate fast, reliable privacy infrastructure for products like
1.1.1.1
Â and
iCloud Private Relay
Â make us a good home for an OHTTP gateway. Because of Cloudflareâs
anycast
Â approach, our OHTTP Gateway will run on every server on Cloudflareâs global edge network, minimizing latency in relay-to-gateway hops. If you use our CDN, user requests can be decrypted by our Gateway and resolved by your app servers on the same Cloudflare metals, saving gateway-to-origin latency.
Finally, recall that OHTTPâs
privacy model
Â requiresÂ that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties. We want to provide our customers with the best possible range of options for their privacy infrastructure. Befo
49941091.article_summary: Cloudflare推出OHTTP Gateway闭测版，并将Privacy Gateway更名为OHTTP Relay。OHTTP通过“中继+网关”两跳架构，将用户身份与请求内容分离，隐藏IP，减轻开发者隐私保护负担。客户可自建网关搭配Cloudflare中继，或使用Cloudflare托管网关搭配第三方中继；其全球边缘网络旨在降低延迟和运维成本。
49941091.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare推出付费OHTTP Gateway后，评论集中于其隐私机制、信任边界、商业动机及滥用治理。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为OHTTP能分离身份与请求内容：Relay知道用户IP，Gateway知道请求但看不到身份，双方无法单独还原完整信息；适合更新检查、隐私分析等场景。  
• 质疑者认为这是把数据从网站日志转移到Cloudflare等大型中心化平台，仍需信任中间方；有人担心其具备“中间人”色彩，甚至认为匿名代理或SOCKS5也能实现类似效果。  
• 有人反对付费隐私功能，认为这会削弱普遍提升隐私的激励；也有人宁愿网站直接看到IP，而不是交给Cloudflare、Google、Meta等巨头。  
• 另一派指出，若网站嵌入Google追踪代码，OHTTP并不能阻止追踪；真正重视隐私的网站应减少第三方网络和行为采集，而非依赖Cloudflare。  
• 安全治理方面，评论担心隐藏IP后难以封禁滥用者、追责攻击来源；在AI代理和自动化滥用增多的情况下，隐私与平台防滥用存在冲突。

补充讨论：争议核心是“减少应用服务器掌握用户身份”是否值得转而信任Cloudflare，以及OHTTP究竟是有效的隐私分权，还是新的集中化数据入口。

data.title: GitHub's new dashboard experience now the default
data.author: vanyauhalin
data.article_summary: GitHub新版仪表板现已默认启用，集中展示活跃代理会话、Issues和Pull Requests，每栏最多显示12项，并支持筛选。用户可在独立的Feed标签查看动态，也能直接分配任务给Copilot编码代理或在Copilot Chat中创建拉取请求。如需使用旧版界面，可通过“Preview”下拉菜单切换。GitHub欢迎用户在社区讨论中反馈意见。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub新版首页/仪表盘是否真正改善信息获取与工作流，以及其功能取舍、可靠性和可定制性。

不同观点：
• **正面认可**：相比以Copilot和社交Feed为主的旧版，新版把个人Issue、PR放在核心位置，更符合“现在要处理什么”的需求；但列表信息密度较低。  
• **希望高度定制**：用户希望固定仓库排序、默认展开更多内容，并能像企业内部缺陷系统一样，以网格和查询组件自定义首页；有人认为个人主页或自建Dashboard更实用。  
• **功能可靠性存疑**：PR收件箱会漏项，不同时间筛选结果不一致；Issue/PR还存在差异显示错误、建议修改不渲染原文、Issue翻页受限等基础Bug。争议焦点是：GitHub不断改UI、推AI，是否应优先修复核心功能。  
• **对AI和Dashboard持怀疑态度**：Copilot无法完成检查依赖等实际任务，却被广泛放置；部分用户认为网页Dashboard是干扰，偏好`gh`命令行、邮件或直接使用Git。  
• **整体体验趋差**：有人认为近几年更新普遍降低可用性，甚至批评GitHub重AI、忽视IPv6；也有人仅提出公告页面文字与背景对比度不足。  

补充讨论：有用户分享通过GitHub Issues、标签、Projects、PR和Actions搭建个人/小团队工作追踪系统，关注AI代理、任务拆分及未来协作管理。

data.title: On building a worm detector
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章提出开发“蚯蚓探测器”，以原位、三维方式绘制农田尺度蚯蚓群落及其运动轨迹。现有研究仅记录地表活动，发现蚯蚓单夜至少可移动约9米。作者认为可结合地质雷达、微波或插入式探针，依据信号变化检测蚯蚓，并结合GPS、土壤湿度和温度等数据建模，从而填补地下生物运动研究的空白。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章引发了对冷门生物知识及相关工具实用性的讨论。

不同观点：
• [andai] 关注文中提到的蚓螈（Caecilians），此前并不了解这种外形类似“蛇和蠕虫”的两栖动物，并对其能分泌类似乳汁、哺育幼体的现象感到惊奇，还提供了百科链接。
• [uriegas] 认为某种“工作检测器”（work detector）可能比预想中更有用，但未进一步说明其具体用途或指代的工具。

补充讨论：两条评论分别从生物学冷知识和工具实用性切入，彼此没有直接回应，讨论较为简短；“工作检测器”的具体含义是潜在的理解重点。

49932509.article_content:
On building a worm detector
25 Sep, 2026
The next frontier in worm research is to be able to visualise (map) the locations of worms, in-situ, and if possible, at the paddock scale.
We know so much more about the movements of ants, spiders, beetles, bees/pollinators and the above ground invertebrates. Yet so little about everything below ground. Frankly its a blight on us all we don't know more. Okay maybe that's a bit dramatic, but for a group of organisms that are so important to soil fertility and health, we know so little about their movements specifically.
Don't get me wrong, many studies have sampled worms out in the field. So we do know about their abundance and diversity in a broad range of ecosystems, especially within agricultural landscapes.
But it's the movement of these worms, both individually and collectively that I wish to understand more. To research this we would have to make some sort of worm detector. Being able to map, not just of one species, but a community of worms in a paddock would be highly valuable data. Currently to my knowledge, there is no method able to capture such worm data.
Its a gap in the research that I am hoping with modern techniques, we may soon be able to investigate further.
My tiny lit review on worm phenomics...
The only study I found that even attempted to record/map the movements of earthworms, in-situ, both as individuals and collectively was by
Mather and Christensen (1988) in Denmark
. They studied
Lumbricus terrestris
, a widely found globally distributed earthworm species (including here in Australia). They studied this species as it regularly surfaces, especially after rain events and forms trails, making it easier to observe/record movements. To my knowledge, this is presently the closest we have got to mapping/visualising worm movements. There probably are more papers on earthworm phenomics, I just haven't had a thorough enough look.
The two authors of this study, Janice Mather and Ole Christensen, the legends that they are, then did a similar experiment
6 years later
, researching the individual movements of the invasive New Zealand Flatworm,
Arthurdendyus triangulatus
, in the Faroe Islands, Denmark. This study differed from the former, in that in the previous study, they measured worm trails using string, but in the latter (in 1994) flatworms were placed on black plastic and their mucus trails were measured with aid of conveniently spaced water droplets.
These were the only two papers I found with any data on the distances traveled by individual worms and both still only measured and recorded above ground movements. With so many advancements in technology, along with advancements in the entire the field of phenomics since these papers, I really feel like its about time we develop some new techniques/methods.
As an aside: How far can an individual earthworm travel?
Well on the night of the 23rd and 24th of October 1987, thirty
L. terrestris
travelled a mean minimum distance of 9.0 m (with a s.d. 3.6 m). The distance individual worms travelled ranged from 3.8 m - 19.3 m in the study area. However, it was because the worms trails moved out of their defined study area (a dirt road) and continued into neighbouring paddocks, that made them unable to measure the full lengths of all worm trails. Further, disturbance made by tractors and footprints also damaged some worm trails. Thus, the estimates are conservative and this is why they are using this mean minimum distance value. In short, we know the average
L. terrestris
can travel at least 9.0m per night (n=30).
What is possible? Ideas on developing such a technology
Immediately I thought of LiDAR. Could we use LiDAR? No, probably not. But instead of sending out pulses of light (which cannot penetrate the ground), what if we use microwaves, or possibly some other wavelength of light? Microwaves is what they use in
ground penetrating radar
. I am currently unsure if ground penetrating radar has enough resolution to detect worms. It's difficult as we need to collect data in three dimentions, and unlike the atmosphere, the ground is very much a solid and not a gas. So maybe we need to stick probes in the ground, to capture the data.
What I imagine is this... Stick a probe in the ground that sends out pulses of a particular wavelength(s). The pulses have known strength and frequency that differ in the absence/presence of worms. How this changes as worm abundance goes from 0 worms, to 1 worm to 10 worms would require prior experimental knowledge. Thereby a probe is able to detect and record any worms nearby, along with GPS data. Do this systematically across a paddock, maybe one probe every 15m or so. Then later on the computer, chuck all this raw data into a model (with callibrations based on the soil types, and maybe other environmental variables, soil moisture/temp etc). You then match this data up spatially, with all the location data. The longitude, latitude and I would say depth, but we need a word for 'neg

data.title: Make Tmux the OS
data.author: weaksauce
data.article_summary: 文章认为，传统桌面窗口管理仍沿用为旧硬件设计的模式，难以适应多显示器、频繁切换设备及不同用户习惯。用户有最大化、近最大化和精细排布等类型，并区分公共与私密窗口；操作系统却无法自动理解显示器角色和工作状态。浏览器也已成为“操作系统中的操作系统”。作者希望借鉴 tmux 的可滚动、持久化、可分离和任务导向体验，设计更适合普通人的未来桌面。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕现代桌面操作系统应如何组织窗口、应用、文件与工作状态，评论者讨论了平铺窗口、虚拟桌面、终端复用器及跨应用“项目流”的优劣。

不同观点：
• **平铺/键盘驱动管理更高效**：有人推荐 Niri、Hyprland、i3、EXWM、Ratpoison、OmniWM 等，认为可减少 macOS/GNOME 中低效的窗口切换；甚至建议把桌面操作能力视为开发者基本素养。  
• **现有工具已部分解决问题**：Tmux、screen、RaceTerm 等可保存会话、抵抗应用崩溃并支持远程续接；但邮件等 HTML 应用难以纳入终端体系。  
• **单纯窗口管理并不足够**：一个工作“流”往往同时涉及邮件、终端、浏览器、笔记和表格，应用之间存在数据孤岛。用户希望操作系统能自动理解并恢复项目、任务及其上下文，而非要求个人手动整理。  
• **持久化应延伸到系统更新**：应允许内核重启后保留用户态会话，避免更新后重新配置全部工作环境。  
• **垂直标签的争议**：有人认可侧边栏标签，但批评 Arc 普及了“列表式”垂直标签，却忽视 Tree Style Tabs 的树状层级和父子关系，导致研究、阅读等场景更不便。  
• **AI与新型桌面设计**：有人设想用小型 LLM 优化窗口布局、选择和切换；也有人认为这类讨论虽与 Tmux 关联有限，但对未来 OS 设计有启发。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“统一、自动化的工作空间”与“用户自行掌握窗口工具”之间的取舍；评论普遍认为不存在适合所有人的方案，但现有桌面体验和文件系统概念仍过于割裂。

49937540.article_content:
I recently watched the talk by Scott Jenson titled "Are we really going to use the same Desktop UX forever?"
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V7AfAcQwLW0&t=445s
. He's a great presenter, really articulate and concise. The kind of speaker that you'd gladly listen to for 3+ hours if given the chance. Which for a talk about window management is quite the compliment.
The overall point of the talk was "Apple and Microsoft aren't going to innovate anymore in the desktop OS space, so it is up to us all to decide what the desktop of the future is going to look like". I would argue that the actual situation to more nuanced than that, they're trying ideas they are just extremely conservative. As Jenson points out, a lot of what we treat as "how computers work" was a workaround for hardware we stopped having years ago. So why are we still accepting those tradeoffs?
To be clear, I'm not a UI/UX designer. I don't know what I'm doing and I lack the skill to make this. I'm making this mostly as a thought exercise and hopefully a prompt to get other people to think about this same problem. I have, however, suffered through others bad choices, which turns out to be most of the qualifications required.
TL;DR: The thing I want is "tmux is the OS", but I want tmux where a normal person could use it. I use it all the time, it's great, but is there a way to take the amazing experience of a scrollable, session-persisted, detachable, task-oriented system to normal people?
What are the high-level problems with windows management in 2026?
I think you can break the problem down to the following components:
My screen real estate is constantly changing and I have a lot more of it.
I am going from my laptop screen to my desktop monitor back to the laptop screen about 6 times a day. When I'm on my big monitor or multiple monitors, overlapping windows don't make sense because I have too much space as it is.
First, one big monitor is a a different experience entirely compared to 2 smaller monitors. I don't use the two monitors as one large unbroken screen, I tend to use one of them for "less important static content" like a ToDo list or my work chat tool and my email and then the "primary" monitor for my terminal/tmux/browser which is how I do all my actual work. But windows "belong" to one or they "belong" to another. Grudin found in 2001 that people use a second monitor exactly this way, where focal work on one, peripheral glances on the other. Twenty-five years ago. The OS still doesn't know which monitor is doing one role and which the other.
And when I pull the laptop out of the dock, everything collapses onto one screen and I manually drag and resize windows to claw back enough real estate to keep working. I don't know how much time this actually wastes for people, but it feels like it wastes a bunch. The OS treats a display change as a surprise, instead of as a scheduled event that happens six times a day.
Different people use windows totally differently.
We have three distinct groups of people that we are trying to design around, while most modern OS optimizes only for the first use case.
Some people are window maximizers, where every window takes up most of the screen and then they use Command + Tab or the Dock or something else to switch between the bigger windows. The value of more screen real estate is mostly that this one big window can be even bigger.
Some people are near maximizers, where one window takes up almost all of the screen real estate, but they'll have one or more smaller windows where they glance at things like status or chat or whatever.
Finally there are people who carefully coordinate all of the windows on their screen.
Almost everyone has "private windows" and "public windows". You are fine with your public windows being lined up and persisting, but you want to hide specific information in other windows from people walking by. The people I complain about are also the people I present quarterly numbers to. I never remember that when I connect my laptop to a display they're going to see my entire screen.
I assumed this was just me with private vs public. But it was measured in 2004, in "Revisiting Display Space Management: Understanding Current Practice to Inform Next-generation Design." Same three types, same public/private split, twenty years ago. See how absolutely none of this is a new idea?
Link
.
Browsers are mini operating systems.
In 2026 everybody quietly agrees that most of your software runs in a browser tab. These web applications will cover a wide variety of use-cases that have historically been owned by local applications. My desktop OS treats a browser just like a normal application, when in fact it is closer to a virtualized OS running inside of my host OS.
Tabs inside of a browser and windows of that browser contain the same level of complexity as my other applications.
Tabs are associated with streams of work alongside my conventional applications. I'm writing Terraform in Vim in my terminal whi
49937540.article_summary: 文章认为，传统桌面窗口管理仍沿用为旧硬件设计的模式，难以适应多显示器、频繁切换设备及不同用户习惯。用户有最大化、近最大化和精细排布等类型，并区分公共与私密窗口；操作系统却无法自动理解显示器角色和工作状态。浏览器也已成为“操作系统中的操作系统”。作者希望借鉴 tmux 的可滚动、持久化、可分离和任务导向体验，设计更适合普通人的未来桌面。
49937540.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕现代桌面操作系统应如何组织窗口、应用、文件与工作状态，评论者讨论了平铺窗口、虚拟桌面、终端复用器及跨应用“项目流”的优劣。

不同观点：
• **平铺/键盘驱动管理更高效**：有人推荐 Niri、Hyprland、i3、EXWM、Ratpoison、OmniWM 等，认为可减少 macOS/GNOME 中低效的窗口切换；甚至建议把桌面操作能力视为开发者基本素养。  
• **现有工具已部分解决问题**：Tmux、screen、RaceTerm 等可保存会话、抵抗应用崩溃并支持远程续接；但邮件等 HTML 应用难以纳入终端体系。  
• **单纯窗口管理并不足够**：一个工作“流”往往同时涉及邮件、终端、浏览器、笔记和表格，应用之间存在数据孤岛。用户希望操作系统能自动理解并恢复项目、任务及其上下文，而非要求个人手动整理。  
• **持久化应延伸到系统更新**：应允许内核重启后保留用户态会话，避免更新后重新配置全部工作环境。  
• **垂直标签的争议**：有人认可侧边栏标签，但批评 Arc 普及了“列表式”垂直标签，却忽视 Tree Style Tabs 的树状层级和父子关系，导致研究、阅读等场景更不便。  
• **AI与新型桌面设计**：有人设想用小型 LLM 优化窗口布局、选择和切换；也有人认为这类讨论虽与 Tmux 关联有限，但对未来 OS 设计有启发。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“统一、自动化的工作空间”与“用户自行掌握窗口工具”之间的取舍；评论普遍认为不存在适合所有人的方案，但现有桌面体验和文件系统概念仍过于割裂。

data.title: Extra Big Ass Intelligence
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个以《蠢蛋进化论》/“超级智能”及现代广告生态为主题的讽刺网站，讨论其创作方式、视觉效果、政治寓意和技术实现。

不同观点：
• 作者称网站是用本地运行的 Qwen 模型生成的恶搞抗议作品，纯属娱乐、不打算盈利；网站意外获得约25万次访问并登上 HN 第一，因 Cloudflare 配额有限可能很快下线。  
• 多数评论认为作品成功讽刺了现实：广告关闭按钮不断移动，被视为现代广告系统和政府设计的“完美写照”；Klarna“餐食广告”等也被认为荒诞得足以成为未来的文化符号。  
• 有人欣赏其 HTML4/Geocities 风格，认为它不像当下泛滥的低质 AI 内容，甚至比现实世界更有“品味”；也有人指出页面本身明显带有 LLM 生成感，形成了意外的反讽。  
• 政治解读较复杂：有人借电影角色 Camacho 对比现实政治人物，认为前者至少愿意听取专家意见；另有人暗示“超级智能”议题可能与为关联人士域名投机有关，并提供事实核查链接。  
• 技术层面存在批评：关闭广告按钮的 CSS 使用了 `right-1`，脚本却修改 `left`，导致按钮变形而非移动；另有人认为应使用 `<marquee>` 标签而不是 CSS 滚动，以保持复古效果。

补充讨论：评论整体以幽默和欣赏为主，但也围绕 AI 创作是否仍算“艺术”、讽刺现实还是被现实反讽，以及政治宣传与商业投机的界限展开。

data.title: Scientists invent underwater umbrellas to protect coral reefs
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过遮挡阳光降低海水温度、缓解珊瑚白化的可行性与局限。

不同观点：
• 支持谨慎应用：BrtByte认为该方法难以覆盖整个珊瑚礁，但可作为热浪期间保护珊瑚苗圃和高价值珊瑚群落的应急措施。  
• 倾向扩大规模：PowerElectronix提出使用大面积漂浮网或遮光结构，认为漂浮装置可能更适合规模化，但也承认目前仍处于早期测试阶段。  
• 质疑可扩展性：Aboutplants认为任何可能大规模推广的方案都可能带来意外后果；refactor_master进一步质疑如何部署覆盖25万平方公里的“水下雨伞”，以及谁会从中获利，关注成本、实施难度和利益分配。  
• 指出根本问题：hackingonempty强调，珊瑚还受到海洋酸化威胁；大气二氧化碳升高会降低海水碱度，影响珊瑚建造骨骼，因此遮光无法解决全部成因。  
• 细节与表达纠正：x______________支持减少直射光，但指出“umbrella”主要是挡雨，“parasol”才是遮光，属于术语层面的挑剔。  
• 归因争议：frunklooper将海洋中的碳排放归咎于“中国船只”，但评论未提供证据，且这一说法把复杂的全球碳排放问题简单化。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于遮光技术究竟是有价值的局部应急手段，还是会因规模、成本、生态副作用而缺乏实际意义；各方也在“缓解症状”和“解决温室气体及海洋酸化根源”之间形成对比。

data.title: Treachery in the Rodin Museum 3D scan verdict
data.author: CosmoWenman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：博物馆高精度文物点云扫描的公开、版权/所有权与公共利益之间的冲突，以及博物馆为何投入大量法律资源阻止发布。

不同观点：
• **反对限制公开**：认为博物馆并未创造文物或扫描对象，不应凭“拥有”数据阻止公众访问；公共博物馆尤其应服务公共领域。有人认为许多雕塑已有全球复制品，博物馆的诉讼是注定失败的“守成”行为。  
• **理解博物馆的商业顾虑**：高质量扫描可让任何人制作复制品，可能削弱博物馆依靠复刻品获得的收入；在现有规则下，公共博物馆可能因此难以生存，甚至有人讽刺建议销毁扫描数据。  
• **质疑法律与制度**：部分评论批评法律论证荒谬、权力机构互相维护，主张以形式化、可验证的规则减少司法任意性。  
• **保持审慎立场**：指出目前主要是单方面报道，博物馆的真实理由和法庭完整论证尚未充分呈现，不能贸然认定其行为不当。

补充讨论：有人询问案件是否会上诉至欧盟层级；拥有博物馆影像的网友则担心将雕塑重建并公开会否遭到跨境下架或诉讼。争议焦点在于：博物馆的经营利益和控制权，是否足以压过公共数据开放与再利用权。

data.title: Bob Cringely Has Died
data.author: paveworld
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕科技作家、评论家Bob Cringely逝世的悼念，以及其对个人电脑和科技行业历史记录、观点传播的贡献。

不同观点：
• 多数评论高度肯定其影响力：有人因《Accidental Empires》（《意外帝国》）了解科技行业并走上编程道路，也有人认为后世将通过他的作品理解个人电脑产业的历史与人物。  
• 许多人欣赏他独立、常带争议的评论风格。《Triumph of the Nerds》及其专栏为远离硅谷的人提供了行业信息；其“不同甚至反主流”的看法拓宽了读者视野。  
• 有评论强调他长期见证并记录科技商业的发展，文章常引发正反两面的讨论，但也因此具有独特价值。  
• 个别评论分享私人回忆：2015年前后他曾访问ZeroTier早期办公室，并评价该项目“本应在十年前就完成”，体现其对新技术的关注。  
• 也有人先核实身份，询问是否为该网站作者Bob Cringely，并提供其个人主页和2020年的相关文章作为线索。

补充讨论：评论整体以悼念和赞誉为主，几乎没有实质性批评；争议焦点主要是他经常引发的正反评价，而非其生平或贡献本身。

data.title: Hole Punch: Sling your spaceship around gravitational fields
data.author: trwhite
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕黑洞引力解谜游戏的趣味性、操作体验、教学设计及玩法扩展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 多数评论认为创意有趣且令人上瘾，称其像“太空高尔夫”，有人通关全部20关，也有人欣赏电脑解法；部分人认为很适合怀旧游戏复兴潮。  
• 操作改进观点：拖拽应设置约5像素的启动阈值，避免误触；首次移动可略有跳跃、之后平滑跟随；光标应及时显示拖拽状态，黑洞不应在拖出区域后沿边缘移动。  
• 移动端体验较差：iPad和手机控制不够精确；拖拽时应隐藏尺寸控件以免遮挡视野，结束后再显示。也有人因不愿横屏而无法体验，反映出设备适配问题。  
• 交互机制存在争议：有人希望通过按钮或长按新增黑洞，避免调整已有黑洞时误添加；也有人指出只能增加质量、不能减重或删除，导致操作失误后难以补救。  
• 教学设计意见分化：有人希望增加可选教学关卡，但也有人认为开场强制帮助信息过多，应该允许玩家自行探索；“快速跳过教程”反而被视为称赞。  
• 关卡与玩法：前八关部分可用最小黑洞完成，有人喜欢这种简洁，也有人期待更复杂的挑战，并提出回合制炮击、动态相空间可视化等扩展。

补充讨论：评论还将作品与《Gravity Assist》、Falstad模拟器等相似项目比较，争议焦点主要是“易上手与自由探索”及“误操作容错率”。

• 教学设计意见分化：有人希望增加可选教学关卡，但也有人认为开场强制帮助信息过多，应该允许玩家自行探索；“快速跳过教程”反而被视为称赞。  
• 关卡与玩法：前八关部分可用最小黑洞完成，有人喜欢这种简洁，也有人期待更复杂的挑战，并提出回合制炮击、动态相空间可视化等扩展。

补充讨论：评论还将作品与《Gravity Assist》、Falstad模拟器等相似项目比较，争议焦点主要是“易上手与自由探索”及“误操作容错率”。

data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Valve工程师Timur Kristóf过去一年持续改进Linux AMDGPU内核驱动，重点支持十年前的AMD GCN 1.0/1.1显卡和APU。他修复显示、功耗管理问题，加入软复位等功能，帮助旧显卡从传统Radeon驱动迁移至AMDGPU，从而支持RADV Vulkan、提升性能与稳定性。相关优化曾带来约30%的性能提升，让老旧AMD显卡在2026年仍能更好地用于Linux游戏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Valve/Steam Deck相关软件与编译器优化如何提升AMD旧款GPU性能，以及这些技术能否扩展到LLM推理。

不同观点：
• [LaurensBER] 认为Linux对Ayaneo 2这类搭载老款移动RDNA 2 GPU的掌机优化出色，许多非新款3A游戏比Windows运行更快更流畅，甚至促使其考虑将主力PC（9070XT）迁移到Linux；他认为Valve的Steam Deck项目及相关贡献功不可没，也赞赏其让旧硬件发挥更大价值。  
• [vkaku] 认为Valve的软件和编译器工作同样能帮助Llama.cpp/GGML等推理项目。Valve在补充AMD ROCm、OpenCL和Vulkan支持方面表现突出，应与AMD合作改进芯片支持。  
• [segmondy] 关注技术向LLM推理迁移的可能性，希望将更多即将成为电子垃圾的旧GPU转化为可用的LLM计算设备。  
• [wewewedxfgdf] 对AMD未能自行完成类似优化表示遗憾，隐含对AMD软件栈和投入不足的批评。  
• [gary_0] 主要提供演讲原视频及时间戳，属于资料补充。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于性能提升究竟更多来自AMD硬件与官方软件，还是Valve主导的Linux、驱动和编译器生态；另一个开放问题是，面向游戏的优化能否有效迁移到通用GPU计算和LLM推理。

49946895.article_content:
The Amazing Work By Valve's Timur Kristóf On Improving Old AMD GPUs On Linux
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Radeon
on 3 October 2026 at 02:56 PM EDT.
13 Comments
Over the past year Timur Kristóf of Valve's Linux graphics driver team has made multiple very nice improvements to the AMDGPU kernel driver for enhancing support for old (GCN 1.0/1.1 era from a decade ago) graphics cards so that they can better handle Linux gaming and other tasks. This week in Toronto, Kristóf presented on this AMDGPU work that he initially began as a kernel driver development exercise after initially spending years in user-space focused on the Mesa 3D driver code.
Timur Kristóf has become a legend for those with old AMD GCN 1.0/1.1 graphics cards and APUs for transitioning them from the legacy Radeon driver over to the modern AMDGPU kernel driver, which unlocks being able to use the RADV Vulkan driver, better performance, and all-around better functionality than the legacy Radeon code. In the process he had to address defects in the AMDGPU display code for these legacy graphics cards along with various power management issues and more. Then he went on to improve these graphics cards further with soft reset support and other enhancements all to make these aging graphics cards more viable for Linux gaming use in 2026 and beyond.
For getting an idea of the impact of transitioning the old Radeon graphics cards to AMDGPU, see last year's
Linux 6.19's Significant ~30% Performance Boost For Old AMD Radeon GPUs
. With AMD not devoting much resources to these aging graphics card driver improvements in years, Timur on Valve's Linux team really picked up the slack to make for a much better experience.
For those wishing to hear him recount his efforts for improving AMD Radeon GCN 1.0/1.1 era graphics on Linux, embedded below is his XDC2026 presentation along with the
PDF slides
. The presentation also goes over his experiences in getting involved in AMDGPU kernel driver development and other tid-bits for those that may want to get involved with the open-source AMD Linux kernel driver development.
